title: Retrofit
objectives: Understand Retrofit (Dart) via a real-life analogy
Generate a typed API client from annotated abstract classes

sections.markdown: **Retrofit (Dart)** is a codegen-based typed HTTP client on top of Dio, inspired by Square's Java Retrofit. You declare an `@RestApi()` abstract class with `@GET/@POST/@PUT/@PATCH/@DELETE` annotated methods; `retrofit_generator` (a `build_runner` builder) emits the concrete class. Typically paired with `json_serializable` for automatic model (de)serialization. Result: **zero boilerplate**, **compile-time-checked API surface**, seamless Dio integration (interceptors, cancellation, mocking still available).

## Common mistakes

**Mistake 1: Forgetting to run `build_runner`.** Any annotation change requires re-generation. Add `build_runner watch` to your dev workflow (or a Melos script). Missing regen = confusing 'method not found' compile errors.

**Mistake 2: `part` directive missing / mismatched.** Both `user.dart` and `api_client.dart` need `part 'X.g.dart';` — otherwise the generated file has no linkage. `.g.dart` files are meant to be checked into git *or* explicitly ignored — pick one policy.

**Mistake 3: Non-nullable field but backend sends null.** `json_serializable` throws at runtime. Prefer nullable fields; use `@JsonKey(defaultValue: ...)` for sensible fallbacks. Model to backend reality.
**Mistake 4: Dynamic runtime path building.** Retrofit only substitutes `{name}` when there's an `@Path() Type name` param. Trying to build the URL manually inside the method defeats the codegen.
**Mistake 5: Interceptors set on the wrong Dio.** Retrofit uses the Dio you pass; if you have two Dio instances (auth + public), you must construct two ApiClients or the wrong interceptors run.
**Mistake 6: Blindly `.toJson()` on Enums.** `json_serializable` needs a `@JsonEnum(valueField: ...)` or a matching `Map<String,dynamic>` extension for enums with values other than name-strings.
**Mistake 7: Not exposing `@CancelRequest()`.** Without it, callers can't cancel — the API surface silently loses a Dio superpower. Add the parameter to every list/search endpoint.
**Mistake 8: Regen conflicts in git.** Two devs regen at the same time → `.g.dart` merge conflicts. Either commit `.g.dart` and coordinate, or `.gitignore` them + regen on CI.
## Best practices
**1. One `ApiClient` per API host.** Different auth = different Dio = different client.
**2. All models with `@JsonSerializable`** + `part` directives + `fromJson/toJson` factories.
**3. Expose `@CancelRequest`** on list / search / detail endpoints.
**4. Idempotency-Key on POST** — `@Header('Idempotency-Key') required String key` on money-moving endpoints.
**5. Nullable fields for backend nulls;** `@JsonKey(defaultValue: ...)` where appropriate.
**6. Split by feature** — one `ApiClient` per feature domain gets busy; a monolithic client also gets ugly. Team convention wins.
**7. `build_runner watch`** in your dev env; CI runs `build_runner build` before analyze/test.
**8. Test with `http_mock_adapter`** — inject a mock Dio into the ApiClient.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Model + ApiClient + one `@GET`; regen; call from `main`.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — `@Path` + `@Query` + `@Body` combo; typed list response.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — `@Header('Idempotency-Key')` on POST; wire caller to pass a UUID.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — `@MultiPart` file upload with `@SendProgress`.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Expose `@CancelRequest` on a search endpoint; cancel on new keystroke.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Migrate a hand-rolled 20-endpoint API client to Retrofit + json_serializable; measure LOC delta + break-change refactor speed.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What problem does Retrofit solve, and how is it different from writing a Dio client by hand?**

**A:** Hand-rolled Dio clients repeat the same shape: build path, encode query, JSON-encode body, dio.request, decode JSON, cast to model. For 40 endpoints that's a lot of near-identical code that drifts from the API contract, forgets to encode a query, and is painful to refactor when the model changes. Retrofit lets you **declare** the API in an abstract class with annotations — path, query, body, headers, multipart, cancel, progress — and `retrofit_generator` (via `build_runner`) emits the concrete calls at build time. Paired with `json_serializable`, (de)serialization is also generated. **Net wins:** ~50% LOC, compile-time-checked API surface (rename a field → compiler catches every caller), easy refactor, single source of truth per endpoint. **Cost:** codegen step in the build; you must remember to run `build_runner` (or use watch mode).

**Q2: Does Retrofit use reflection at runtime?**

**A:** **No.** Dart AOT prohibits `dart:mirrors`; Retrofit is entirely **compile-time codegen**. `retrofit_generator` reads your `.dart` files at build time, walks the annotation AST, and emits a `.g.dart` file with a concrete class implementing your abstract API. At runtime, the generated code is plain method calls on `Dio` — no reflection, no dynamic dispatch, no runtime cost beyond Dio itself. This is different from Java's Retrofit, which does use reflection + dynamic proxies at runtime. Consequence: any annotation change requires regen; but there's zero runtime overhead + full AOT compatibility (safe for Flutter release builds).

**Q3: How do you handle cancellation + progress with Retrofit?**

**A:** Expose `@CancelRequest() CancelToken? cancel` as an optional named parameter on the interface method. Retrofit's codegen passes it through to Dio's `RequestOptions`. Caller creates a token, passes it, cancels in `dispose`. For progress: `@SendProgress() ProgressCallback? onSendProgress` and `@ReceiveProgress() ProgressCallback? onReceiveProgress` — Dio wires them to the underlying `HttpClient` byte counters, and you update a `ValueNotifier<double>` for the UI. Also `@DioOptions() Options? options` if you need per-call `receiveTimeout` override or `extra: {'tenantId': ...}` for interceptors. Interviewers love hearing that **cancellation is exposed at the API surface** — an ApiClient without it forces UI code to leak requests.

**Q4: json_serializable throws on a real API response — walk through diagnosis and fix.**

**A:** Typical bugs: **(1) Backend sends null for a non-nullable Dart field** → runtime `TypeError`. Fix: make field nullable OR add `@JsonKey(defaultValue: ...)`. **(2) Field name mismatch** — API sends `snake_case`, model has `camelCase` — enable `@JsonSerializable(fieldRename: FieldRename.snake)` or annotate individual fields with `@JsonKey(name: 'user_id')`. **(3) Enum value mismatch** — API sends `'ACTIVE'`, enum is `active` — `@JsonEnum(valueField: 'value')` or use a custom `_$MyEnumEnumMap`. **(4) Nested object null** — parent decodes but nested `.fromJson` throws — the fix is usually a nullable nested field. **(5) DateTime format** — API sends `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`, `json_serializable` handles it; API sends `1234567890` (epoch) — write a converter via `@JsonKey(fromJson: fromEpoch, toJson: toEpoch)`. **Debugging tip:** temporarily change the model field to `dynamic`, log the value, see the shape, then type it correctly.

**Q5: Would you commit generated `.g.dart` files or gitignore them?**

**A:** **Trade-off — both are valid.** **Commit** if: team is small, everyone always regens locally, generated code is stable → PR reviewers can see the emitted surface. **Gitignore** if: team is large, generated files churn, merge conflicts on `.g.dart` are frequent → run `build_runner build` in CI as a pre-analyze step + as a preinstall hook post-clone. **Also affects:** IDE — some IDEs need the `.g.dart` present to resolve types; if gitignored, run `build_runner` after clone. **Most large teams** gitignore `.g.dart` + `.freezed.dart` and enforce CI regen. **Small teams** commit them for reviewability. **Wrong answer:** 'always commit' or 'always ignore' — team convention wins; document it.

**Q6: How does Retrofit interact with Dio interceptors + tests?**

**A:** Retrofit uses **whichever Dio you pass** at construction — `ApiClient(dio)`. All interceptors on that Dio (auth, retry, log, cache) apply transparently to every generated call. **Multiple Dios** = multiple ApiClients (auth vs public API). **Testing:** inject a Dio built with `DioAdapter` (from `http_mock_adapter`), which returns canned responses. The generated `_ApiClient` calls `dio.fetch` under the hood — the mock adapter intercepts. Unit tests can now verify high-level behavior (`api.listUsers()` returns typed `List<User>`) without touching real HTTP. **Also:** interceptor `RequestOptions.extra` — use `@DioOptions() Options? options` to pass `extra: {'skipAuth': true}` for endpoints that shouldn't get the Bearer (login, refresh).

## Real-world usage

- **Every large Flutter codebase** with a well-defined REST API — banking, e-commerce, delivery.
- **OpenAPI-first teams** — generate models with `openapi_generator`; hand-write Retrofit interfaces or generate them.
- **Micro-services** — one ApiClient per micro-service, each with its own baseUrl + interceptor stack.
- **Testing** — `http_mock_adapter` on a Dio injected into ApiClient.
- **NOT ideal for** — WebSocket / gRPC / GraphQL (use dedicated clients like `graphql_flutter`).

## Advanced notes

- **`@DioOptions() Options?`** — pass per-call `receiveTimeout` / `extra` / `responseType` from the call site.
- **`@ParseErrorLogger`** — Retrofit v4+ supports pluggable error loggers; wire to Crashlytics.
- **`@Extras()`** — key-value map into `RequestOptions.extra` — visible to interceptors.
- **Custom converters** — for non-JSON responses (protobuf, msgpack); implement your own `Parser`.
- **`@Preserve()` / `@GenericConverter()`** for generics + polymorphism.
- **`retrofit_generator` versus `chopper`** — Chopper takes a similar codegen approach but is `http`-backed; Retrofit-Dart wins on Dio ecosystem.
- **OpenAPI codegen** — `openapi-generator-cli` can emit Retrofit-Dart-style clients directly; useful for large APIs with 100s of endpoints.
- **`retrofit_gen`'s error handling** — non-200s bubble as `DioException`; map centrally.
- **Multiple base URLs at runtime** — pass a mutable `baseUrl` to `factory ApiClient(Dio, {String? baseUrl})`.
- **JSON polymorphism** — use `@JsonKey(fromJson: X, toJson: Y)` + a manual type discriminator; `freezed` unions offer nicer syntax.
- **freezed integration** — Freezed models + json_serializable + Retrofit is the common combo; Freezed emits `.freezed.dart` + `.g.dart` alongside.
